title: Injectivity of the transcript pull-back
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be maps on the input spaces. Consider the pulled-back protocol over $X' \times Y'$ obtained by pre-composing every message function of $p$ with $f_X$ or $f_Y$ as appropriate. Then the map that sends each syntactic transcript of $p$ to the corresponding transcript of this pulled-back protocol — preserving the sequence of Boolean messages while re-routing through the input maps — is injective.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic protocol p over input types X, Y with output type α
input maps f_X : X' → X and f_Y : Y' → Y
replaced:
For every protocol $p$ and input maps $f_X : X' \to X$, $f_Y : Y' \to Y$, the map
\texttt{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.transcriptComap}~$p$~$f_X$~$f_Y$ from $\mathrm{Transcript}(p)$ to
$\mathrm{Transcript}(p.\mathrm{comap}(f_X, f_Y))$ is injective.
